record.paper_title: Some Open Questions in Wave Chaos
record.context_brief: QUE for non-arithmetic negatively curved manifolds
record.original_question: Can Quantum Unique Ergodicity be proved for non-arithmetic negatively curved surfaces and higher-dimensional negatively curved manifolds, meaning that every high-energy semiclassical measure μ_k of Laplacian eigenfunctions converges to the Liouville measure μ_L rather than only a full-density subsequence? If a full proof is unavailable, what restrictions can be proved on all possible invariant limit measures?

evidence.quote: Rudnick and Sarnak have conjectured that exceptional sequences cannot exist on negatively curved manifolds [27] (that is, the full sequence (µ k)k∈N converges to µ L), this property being called “Quantum Unique Ergodicity” (QUE).
The QUE conjecture is still wide open for non-arithmetic surfaces (and higher-dimensional manifolds).
Rather than proving that all semiclassical measures converge to µ L, one can at least try to obtain some information on the possible limit measures.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g)$ be a smooth compact Riemannian manifold of negative sectional curvature (in particular, the geodesic flow on the unit cotangent bundle $S^*M$ is Anosov). Let $\Delta_g$ denote the (positive) Laplace–Beltrami operator on $M$, and let $(\varphi_k)_{k\in\mathbb{N}}$ be an orthonormal basis of $L^2(M)$ consisting of eigenfunctions $\Delta_g \varphi_k = \lambda_k \varphi_k$ with $\lambda_k \to \infty$.

To each eigenfunction $\varphi_k$ associate its microlocal lift, a distribution $\tilde{\mu}_k$ on $S^*M$ such that for every classical symbol $a \in C_c^\infty(T^*M)$,
$$\langle \mathrm{Op}_{\hbar_k}(a)\varphi_k, \varphi_k\rangle \longrightarrow \int_{S^*M} a\, d\mu \quad (\hbar_k = \lambda_k^{-1/2}),$$
along subsequences, where $\mu$ is a probability measure on $S^*M$ invariant under the geodesic flow $\Phi^t$. Such limit measures $\mu$ are called semiclassical (quantum) limit measures. Let $\mu_L$ denote the normalized Liouville measure on $S^*M$.

(a) Prove the Quantum Unique Ergodicity (QUE) conjecture for $(M,g)$ when $M$ is not an arithmetic surface (and more generally when $M$ is a higher-dimensional negatively curved manifold without arithmetic structure): show that the full sequence of microlocal lifts $\tilde{\mu}_k$ converges weakly-$*$ to $\mu_L$ as $k\to\infty$, rather than merely along a density-one subsequence.

(b) In the absence of a full proof of (a), establish nontrivial restrictions on the set of all possible $\Phi^t$-invariant probability measures $\mu$ on $S^*M$ that arise as semiclassical limits (for instance bounds on their Kolmogorov–Sinai entropy, lower bounds on the Hausdorff dimension of their support, or constraints on their pure-point/singular components).
artifact.status_search_result: The Rudnick–Sarnak QUE conjecture remains open for general non-arithmetic negatively curved surfaces and higher-dimensional negatively curved manifolds. It has been proved in the arithmetic setting (Lindenstrauss for compact arithmetic surfaces, Soundararajan for the modular surface), and partial results exist in the general case via entropy bounds of Anantharaman, Anantharaman–Nonnenmacher, and Dyatlov–Jin–Nonnenmacher (full support / positive entropy of quantum limits). Recent progress (e.g., 2024 work on non-escape of mass for arithmetic hyperbolic 4-manifolds) is restricted to the arithmetic side; the non-arithmetic case is still wide open.

status_evidence.title: Recent progress on the quantum unique ergodicity conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: For general (non-arithmetic) manifolds tools are limited to microlocal analysis and dynamics of the geodesic flow; for arithmetic manifolds the basic conjecture has been resolved.
status_evidence.claim: QUE is established in arithmetic cases but remains open for non-arithmetic negatively curved manifolds.

status_evidence.title: Non-escape of mass for arithmetic quantum limits on hyperbolic 4-manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: Progress on QUE in the arithmetic setting on hyperbolic 4-manifolds (eliminating escape of mass for Hecke–Maass forms).
status_evidence.claim: Recent QUE progress is in the arithmetic setting, not for general non-arithmetic manifolds.

status_evidence.title: Background on the QUE conjecture (AIM)
status_evidence.snippet: Rudnick–Sarnak conjectured QUE for compact negatively curved manifolds; for most hyperbolic surfaces QUE is far from proven.
status_evidence.claim: The QUE conjecture for general negatively curved manifolds is still far from proven.
